conventions.convention: The exterior has M>0, 0<|Q|<M, r>r₊, signature (−+++), electric gauge A=−Q dt/r, and charged derivative D=∂−ieA. The frequency ω is real and positive.
The tortoise coordinate is the oriented integral of 1/f from 2r₊ to r, with range ℝ. Infinity uses the Coulomb phase Θ=ωr_*−eQ log(r/L), including separately prescribed derivative asymptotics.

Φ_H=Q/r₊ is a difference of endpoint limits, and ω_H=ω−eΦ_H. The horizon asymptotic branch is exp(−iω_Hr_*); at ω_H=0 it does not distinguish incoming and outgoing directions. Scattering admissibility alone asserts neither existence nor uniqueness.
The harmonic is supplied, smooth, real, and normalized by ∫Y²=1, with eigenvalue −ℓ(ℓ+1). Geometric units use length coordinates, [e]=[ω]=m⁻¹, and dimensionless R,T.

The conserved mathematical radial flux is j=Im(conjugate(u)u′). Its incident and reflected magnitudes at infinity are ω and ω|R|²; identification with physical energy flux requires a separate tensor calculation and adopted model.

load_bearing.statement: Defines the fixed subextremal electric RN exterior, charged wave operator, supplied angular harmonic, normalized separated mode, Coulomb-phase infinity asymptotics and horizon asymptotics, including their differentiated forms. These define admissible data without asserting existence or uniqueness.
Every admitted scattering solution has constant j=Im(conjugate(u)u′) and |R|²=1−(ω−eQ/r₊)|T|²/ω. Consequently 0<ω<eQ/r₊ and T≠0 imply |R|²>1, conditional on an admitted solution.
Under the exact scattering-definition conventions, every smooth separated charged-wave solution satisfies u″+[(ω−eQ/r)²−f(ℓ(ℓ+1)/r²+f′/r)]u=0, with primes on u taken in r_* and f′ taken in r.

seams_checked.note: The charged-scattering definition uses the draft neutral RN scalar-coordinate lemma for the identical subextremal electric specialization, integral basepoint, smooth coordinate and endpoint limits. The charged radial equation is calculated locally; no neutral energy estimate is promoted to a charged or coupled stability result.

The test-field postulate, asymptotic energy-flux lemma and conditional amplification theorem preserve the gauge, endpoint potential difference, Coulomb phase, normalized asymptotics and conditional existence status. A separate stress-tensor calculation establishes the energy-flux ratio |R|². The amplification theorem retains the strict frequency band and T≠0; the postulate's extremal branch is explicitly excluded from its scattering consequences.
